# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

1800-180-1551 (Kisan Call Centre) / 1076 (CM Helpline); Deputy Director Agriculture office in your district
UP BOCW Shramik Panjikaran (Construction Worker Labour Card)
Uttar Pradesh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (UPBOCW), Labour Department

Registering with the UP construction workers' board gives a construction worker a labour card. The card opens the family's main benefits: Rs.65,000 for a daughter's marriage, money at childbirth, school and college help for two children, a Rs.1,000 monthly pension after 60, and up to Rs.5 lakh if the worker dies in an accident. Masons, helpers, carpenters, bar benders, plumbers, electricians, painters, tile workers and road and building labourers can all register. You register online with Aadhaar e-KYC (or at a CSC) and renew the card to keep the benefits.
Rs.65,000 for a daughter's marriage, Rs.20,000–25,000 at childbirth, Rs.1,000 monthly pension, Rs.5 lakh on accidental death
Has done at least 90 days of building or other construction work in the last 12 months
Works in Uttar Pradesh and is not registered with the construction board of another state
Pays a Rs.20 registration fee once, plus Rs.20 for each year of membership chosen (1, 2 or 3 years). One year costs Rs.40 in all
Most benefits (marriage, maternity, serious illness) start after 1 year of membership. The pension needs 10 years of membership and age 60
Benefits go to at most two children, and you must apply within 1 year of the event
Aadhaar card, with OTP on the Aadhaar-linked mobile for e-KYC
Certificate of 90 days of work from the contractor or employer, or the board's self-declaration form
Family ID or ration card, to add family members
Bank passbook of an account in the worker's own name
The worker's own Aadhaar. Your name, date of birth and address are filled in from Aadhaar after the OTP.
The OTP goes to the mobile linked with Aadhaar. If that number is lost, get it updated at an Aadhaar centre first.
Your Aadhaar-linked number or any other number you keep. The approval SMS and login messages come here.
Pick Family ID or Ration Card, enter the number, and the family members appear. Tick each member who should be linked to your card.
Where you live and work now, if it is different from the address on Aadhaar.
The construction work you actually do, for example helper, carpenter, plumber, painter or bar bender.
It must be 90 days or more. The work certificate you upload has to show the same number.
The contractor or employer who gave you the 90-day certificate. The office may call this number.
Your own account. Benefit money is paid only by DBT into this account.
Choose 1, 2 or 3 years. Each year costs Rs.20 more. The Rs.20 registration fee is paid only once.
Open labour.upbocw.in and tap Register. Enter your Aadhaar number, tick the consent and verify with the OTP. Your details come from Aadhaar. Then enter a mobile number and set a password.
Log in and complete each part of the profile: personal details, family ID or ration card members, present address, work details and bank details.
Upload your photo and the 90-day work certificate, then tick the self-declaration.
Choose 1, 2 or 3 years and pay the fee online. Save the application number and the payment receipt.
The Labour Enforcement Officer at the district labour office checks the application. You get an SMS when it is approved.
Log in and download your labour card. Renew it up to one month before it expires, because benefits stop on an expired card.
After one year of membership, apply for benefits (daughter's marriage, maternity, children's education) from the same login or at a CSC, within 1 year of the event.
1800-180-5412 (UPBOCW toll-free); district Labour Office (Shram Karyalaya)
Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Abhiyan (MMJAA Ayushman Card)
State Agency for Comprehensive Health and Integrated Services (SACHIS), Medical Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh

Uttar Pradesh's own health cover for poor families who were left out of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. It gives the same Rs.5 lakh a year of free, cashless hospital treatment for the whole family at empanelled government and private hospitals, fully paid by the state. Covered families get the same Ayushman card, made free on the Ayushman portal or app, at a CSC, or at the Ayushman Mitra desk of an empanelled hospital. It has run since 1 March 2019 and is managed by SACHIS.
Rs.5 lakh a year per family, cashless, same as the Ayushman card
Poor families who should have been covered by PM-JAY but were missed in the SECC 2011 list, and were later found in the state's own surveys
All Antyodaya (AAY) ration card families of Uttar Pradesh, added in July 2021
Construction workers registered with the UP BOCW board, and other groups the state government notifies
There is no limit on family size or age. Illnesses you already have are covered from day one
You cannot sign up on your own: the family's name must already be in the list. Check with Am I Eligible on the Ayushman portal or call 1800-1800-4444
Everyone aged 70 and above, whatever the income, gets the separate Ayushman Vay Vandana card
Aadhaar card of the member whose card is being made
Ration card (Antyodaya) or UP Family ID, to find the family in the list
Labour card, if the family is covered as a registered construction worker
Any working number you keep. The login OTP and the approval message come here.
Choose the state Uttar Pradesh. State scheme families are searched from the same Ayushman list. If MMJAA appears in the scheme list for UP, choose that.
Antyodaya families can search by ration card number. Others can search by Aadhaar, Family ID or name.
Copy it from the ration card. If nothing is found, search again with the Aadhaar number of the head of the family.
The Aadhaar of the member whose card you are making now. Each member is done one at a time.
Use Aadhaar OTP if the mobile is linked to Aadhaar. Otherwise choose face authentication on the phone camera.
Good light, face straight, no cap or dark glasses. A blurred photo gets rejected.
Where you actually live now, so the nearest empanelled hospitals are shown.
Open beneficiary.nha.gov.in, log in as Beneficiary with your mobile number and OTP, choose Uttar Pradesh, and search for your family by ration card, Aadhaar or Family ID.
If your family's names appear, you are covered, whether under PM-JAY or the state's MMJAA. The card and the hospital benefit are the same.
Tap the Aadhaar icon next to a member marked eKYC pending, verify with an Aadhaar OTP or face authentication, take the live photo and fill in the relation, district and PIN code.
Submit. SACHIS usually approves it within a day or two. Then open Download Card, verify with OTP and save the card on your phone.
If your family is not found, ask at the Ayushman Mitra desk of the nearest government hospital or at a CSC, or call 1800-1800-4444. A family that is not in the list cannot be added online.
1800-1800-4444 (SACHIS, Uttar Pradesh toll-free) / 14555 (national Ayushman helpline)
Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (Kanya Sumangala)
Directorate of Women Welfare, Department of Women & Child Development, Government of Uttar Pradesh

Rs.25,000 for a daughter, paid in six parts from her birth until she joins college, straight into the mother's bank account (the father's or guardian's if the mother is not alive). The family applies online at each stage: birth, full vaccination, and admission to Class 1, Class 6, Class 9 and a degree or diploma. The total was raised from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 from 1 April 2024.
The family lives permanently in Uttar Pradesh and has proof of residence
Family income is up to Rs.3 lakh a year

Mukhyamantri Samuhik Vivah Yojana (Samuhik Vivah)
Social Welfare Department (Samaj Kalyan Vibhag), Government of Uttar Pradesh

The UP government spends Rs.1 lakh on each couple married at a mass wedding it organises. Rs.64,000 goes into the bride's bank account, Rs.21,000 is given as household gifts and Rs.15,000 pays for the ceremony. The total was earlier Rs.51,000. It is for brides from poor families of every religion with income up to Rs.3 lakh a year, and also for widowed, abandoned or legally divorced women who are remarrying. The bride applies online with her Aadhaar, and the wedding is held at a block, town or district mass wedding run by the District Social Welfare Officer.
Rs.1,00,000 per couple: Rs.64,000 to the bride's account, Rs.21,000 in gifts, Rs.15,000 for the ceremony
The bride's parents or guardians are permanent residents of Uttar Pradesh. The bride herself must be an adult and applies herself
The family is poor or needy, with income up to Rs.3 lakh a year
On the wedding date the bride is at least 18 and the groom at least 21
The bride is unmarried, or is a widow, an abandoned woman or a legally divorced woman who is remarrying
SC, ST and OBC applicants must give a caste certificate. Orphan girls, daughters of widows or disabled parents, and girls with a disability get priority
She must not take marriage money from any other central or state scheme for this wedding

Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana (Ayushman Golden Card)
State Health Authority, Uttarakhand (Medical Health & Family Welfare Department)

Free, cashless hospital treatment up to Rs 5 lakh a year per family for almost every family in Uttarakhand. Families on the central PM-JAY list are covered by PM-JAY, and the state covers all the other resident families under Atal Ayushman on the same terms, hospitals and packages. The Ayushman (golden) card is made from your ration card or family register, on the phone or at a Jan Seva Kendra (CSC).
Uttarakhand families found in any of these lists: NFSA ration card data, the old Mukhyamantri Swasthya Bima Yojana, SECC 2011 or SECC Plus
No income limit and no limit on family size; every member is covered
Not for people covered by CGHS, ECHS, ESIC or the State Government Health Scheme (state employees and pensioners have their own SGHS card)
Illnesses you already have are covered from day one
Atal Ayushman uses a referral system, so planned treatment at a private hospital may first need a referral from a government hospital
Family ID: ration card (new or old) or a copy of the family register (Parivar Register)
If you have neither: an ID such as voter ID, birth certificate, permanent residence certificate, PAN or passport showing your father's, mother's or spouse's name
